title: Graph-Recurrent Learning of Emergent Collective Dynamics
authors: Ali Rayat, Acacia Lee, Gia-Wei Chern
abstract: Collective ordering in correlated electron systems emerges from microscopic dynamics, yet the evolution of observable textures need not admit a closed, memoryless description. We introduce a graph-recurrent neural network (GRNN) framework that learns such emergent dynamics directly from trajectories without specifying microscopic equations of motion. The framework integrates gated recurrent memory with graph message passing: local hidden states encode information beyond the instantaneous observables, while spatial coupling allows this information to propagate between sites. The observable and hidden fields evolve jointly through a shared local rule, providing a scalable representation of dynamics with spatial interactions and temporal memory. We demonstrate this framework on the emergent dynamics of charge-density-wave order in the semiclassical Holstein model, successfully reproducing temporal and spatial correlations and dynamical scaling during domain coarsening. By learning finite-time evolution directly, the GRNN offers a route to efficient, data-driven descriptions of collective dynamics with unresolved microscopic degrees of freedom.
summary: This paper proposes a Graph-Recurrent Neural Network (GRNN) to model the complex, memory-dependent dynamics of collective order parameters in correlated electron systems. By learning the evolution directly from trajectories, the GRNN bypasses the need for explicit, closed-form equations of motion. The framework successfully reproduces the characteristic scaling and correlations observed during CDW domain coarsening in the Holstein model.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing efficient, data-driven methods to describe emergent collective dynamics in correlated electron systems where the observable evolution lacks a simple, closed, memoryless description.
main_result: The proposed Graph-Recurrent Neural Network (GRNN) successfully reproduces key dynamical features, such as temporal and spatial correlations and dynamical scaling, observed during charge-density-wave domain coarsening.
method: A Graph-Recurrent Neural Network (GRNN) is introduced, which integrates gated recurrent memory with graph message passing to learn the time evolution directly from system trajectories without needing explicit microscopic equations of motion.
model_or_system: The framework is demonstrated on the emergent dynamics of charge-density-wave (CDW) order within the semiclassical Holstein model, which describes correlated electron systems on a lattice.
key_observables: Temporal autocorrelation function $A(\tau)$, spatial correlation function $C(R, t)$, and the characteristic domain size $L(t)$.
important_parameters: The system involves parameters like hopping ($t_{nn}$), electron-lattice coupling ($g$), and elastic interactions ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the adiabatic approximation for the lattice dynamics and assumes the GRNN can encode the influence of unresolved microscopic degrees of freedom via its hidden state.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the GRNN prediction against the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) reference for the normalized temporal autocorrelation $A(\tau)$. Figure 3 compares spatial correlation functions $C(R, t)$ showing dynamical scaling. Figure 4 shows the simulation of CDW domain coarsening.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the GRNN framework, details its coupled evolution of physical ($\phi$) and hidden ($h$) states, and then applies it to the Holstein model. The results are validated by comparing predicted dynamics against established reference methods like KPM, and an ablation study confirms the necessity of spatial coupling in the recurrent structure.
why_interesting: The use of ML to model non-Markovian, emergent dynamics in condensed matter systems is highly relevant. It offers a powerful, data-driven alternative to solving complex, coupled differential equations, particularly useful for systems where the full microscopic Hamiltonian is intractable.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the graph-recurrent update. The upper lattices represent successive physical configurations ϕ(t), and the lower lattices represent the corresponding site-resolved hidden states h(t). The labels t −1, t, and t + 1 denote successive prediction steps. Neighboring sites contribute to both the spatial representation of the physical field and the evolution of the hidden states. The colored arrows indicate the exchange of information between the physical and hidden states. The schematic shows the coupled evolution; the oper- ations within one time step are given in the text.

FIG. 2. Normalized temporal autocorrelation A(τ) of the CDW order parameter, comparing GRNN predictions (green) with reference adiabatic dynamics computed using KPM (ma- genta). The GRNN closely reproduces the decay of temporal correlations over the full interval 0 ≤τ ≤400.

FIG. 3. Equal-time CDW correlation function C(R, t) ver- sus scaled separation R = x/L(t) at t = 40, 80, 160, and 320, obtained from KPM reference dynamics (left) and GRNN pre- dictions (right). The GRNN captures the spatial correlation profiles, while the collapse of curves at different times in both panels demonstrates dynamical scaling.

FIG. 4. Autoregressive GRNN simulation of CDW domain coarsening on a 200 × 200 lattice at t = 0, 80, and 6400. Color indicates the local order parameter ϕ on the scale shown at right, from −1 to 1. The initially disordered field evolves into domains of the two symmetry-related charge-ordered states.
